eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on a 26°C-or-higher maximum for Mexico City on September 2 reflects official post-event meteorological observations confirming the daily high reached or exceeded that threshold. This consensus, supported by recent observations near 30–31°C and typical early-September climatology, underpins the market’s 95.5% implied probability for that exact threshold. Afternoon instability and modest wind speeds reduce the chance of localized spikes above 32°C. A stronger high-pressure ridge or unexpected clearing could push readings higher, while heavier rain bands might cap the maximum below 31°C, though current model agreement makes such shifts unlikely before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Tropical cyclone Saudel crossing eastern Guangdong and the combined influence of the northeast monsoon are the dominant factors capping Hong Kong’s maximum temperature near 29–30 °C on September 3.** Official Hong Kong Observatory guidance forecasts 26–31 °C under northwest winds of force 4–5 (locally 6 offshore and on high ground), with partly sunny conditions giving way to one or two showers and persistent cloud cover. Real-time station readings through midday show peaks of 29–30.9 °C at urban and airport sites, with higher-elevation and wind-exposed locations remaining several degrees cooler. These conditions align with model consensus that moderate winds and moisture limit surface heating despite September’s climatological baseline near 31 °C. Traders have priced the 29 °C and 30 °C bins at 55 % and 37 % respectively, reflecting the narrow window between the official upper forecast bound and the suppressing effects of the cyclone and monsoon flow; any late-day clearing or model shift could still push the daily maximum to the 31 °C threshold.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Shanghai Pudong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zspd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The slight edge for 32 °C versus 33 °C arises from minor differences in model timing of the daily maximum and the precise influence of Beijing’s urban heat island, which can add 1–2 °C locally. Historical climatology places the September 3 average high at roughly 28.6 °C, so today’s elevated readings represent above-normal late-summer warmth without extreme heatwave drivers. With the day’s peak likely occurring in the next few hours and resolution based on official meteorological service maxima, traders are weighting the most recent observational trends and ensemble spread to differentiate the two leading outcomes.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Esenboğa Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ltac

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus centers on 30°C as Munich's peak temperature for September 4, with 29°C a close second, reflecting tight ensemble spreads in the latest ECMWF and ICON model runs that place maximums near the 29–30°C threshold under a weakening high-pressure ridge. Warm southerly advection and limited cloud cover are expected to support daytime heating, while urban heat-island effects at the official measurement site could add 0.5–1°C locally; however, any increase in boundary-layer moisture or earlier onset of afternoon convection would cap readings closer to 29°C. Historical September baselines for Munich average 20–22°C, making this outlier warmth notable. Updated high-resolution model guidance and official DWD forecasts issued overnight will likely refine the final outcome before markets close.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus across multiple models positions 32°C as the most likely daily high for Tel Aviv on September 4, 2026, driving the 70% market-implied probability.** Official and ensemble guidance from sources such as the Met Office, Meteoprog, and regional numerical weather prediction runs indicate a maximum near 31–32°C under mostly clear skies, light westerly winds of 5–10 km/h, and negligible precipitation. Typical late-summer Mediterranean conditions—stable subtropical high pressure, low cloud cover, and seasonal sea-surface temperatures around 28–29°C—support this range without significant diurnal amplification or cooling from advection. Recent model runs show minimal spread, with only modest 1°C uncertainty tied to exact timing of peak insolation and boundary-layer mixing. Historical September climatology for Tel Aviv (average high ~31°C) further anchors trader expectations around these values, while the low probabilities assigned to 33°C or 31°C reflect the narrow forecast envelope and limited upside potential absent unexpected synoptic shifts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Wuhan Tianhe International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zhhh

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from Chinese meteorological sources and international models points to a daytime high of 32–33°C in Chengdu on September 4, driven by continued influence of the western Pacific subtropical high that has sustained clear to partly cloudy skies and light northerly winds over the past week. These conditions promote strong solar heating during peak afternoon hours while limiting moisture and cloud cover that would otherwise cap temperatures. Recent observations show daily maxima of 33–35°C in early September, consistent with the seasonal transition before the onset of Huaxi autumn rainfall expected later in the month. Minor model spread centers on the precise timing and extent of any western mountain showers, which could trim the urban high by 1°C if they spread eastward more than anticipated. Trader emphasis on 33–34°C outcomes reflects this narrow uncertainty band ahead of final observational data.

High humidity near 70–80% and residual moisture from recent convective activity further moderate peak readings below the September climatological average of 31°C. eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon activity, recently enhanced by Tropical Storm Pilandok as it exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility on September 3, drives widespread cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and heavy rainfall across Manila on September 4. Official PAGASA guidance and multiple forecast models indicate daytime maxima near 29–30°C amid high humidity and moderate-to-strong southwesterly winds, below the typical September average high of about 31°C. These conditions suppress peak heating through reduced solar insolation and evaporative cooling from precipitation, creating tight uncertainty around whether the daily maximum reaches 30°C or 31°C. Model consensus on rain timing and intensity will determine the outcome, with fresh PAGASA updates and observational data releases likely to refine trader positioning before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance point to a peak temperature near 31–32°C in Panama City on September 4, aligning with the market’s leading outcomes at 44% for 32°C and 23% each for 31°C and 33°C.** 

In early September, Panama lies in the wet season under the influence of the Intertropical Convergence Zone, where frequent afternoon convection, high humidity, and widespread cloud cover typically cap daytime maxima. Recent model runs from GFS and ECMWF show scattered to numerous thunderstorms, which reduce solar insolation and limit surface heating compared with drier periods. Historical climatology places average September highs near 31°C, with observed values rarely exceeding 33°C absent strong subsidence. The narrow spread between the top three outcomes reflects this tight clustering around the seasonal mean, tempered by minor uncertainties in exact cloud timing and rainfall distribution that could nudge the daily maximum by 1°C either way before final observations are recorded.

eventMetadata.context_description: Singapore’s equatorial climate produces consistently high humidity and limited seasonal temperature swings, with September averages near 31.6°C and historical daily maxima rarely exceeding 34–35°C absent unusual atmospheric conditions. Current numerical weather models from multiple agencies converge on a September 5 high around 31–32°C under southeasterly flow and partly cloudy skies, with only modest afternoon heating expected before typical convective showers develop. The near-even market split between 38°C+ and 28°C-or-below outcomes therefore captures traders’ recognition that small shifts in cloud cover, moisture convergence, or model bias could push the observed maximum a few degrees in either direction, while the flat pricing across intermediate bins reflects the narrow historical distribution around the mean. Updated local observations and the next model runs will clarify whether steering patterns or localized heating alter this baseline.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest forecast consensus from models including those referenced by the Met Office and European meteorological services indicates a peak temperature of 33–35°C in Milan on September 5 under a stable high-pressure ridge delivering clear skies and light winds. With the target date only two days away, model spread remains narrow, limiting upside or downside surprises unless an unexpected frontal passage develops. Traders appear to price elevated outcomes accordingly, reflecting the strong observational and dynamical support for continued warmth through the weekend.

Trader sentiment remains balanced across the 35–43°C bins because short-range model spreads and subtle variations in boundary-layer mixing create genuine uncertainty in the precise daily high, with resolution hinging on the final observational maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon flows, recently enhanced by Tropical Storm Pilandok before its exit from the Philippine Area of Responsibility, are driving extensive cloud cover, convection, and widespread rainfall across Metro Manila through early September. Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble model runs indicate daytime highs near 29–30 °C on September 5, with near-100 % precipitation probability suppressing surface heating compared with climatological September averages around 31 °C. These conditions align with seasonal expectations for the habagat period and limit the potential for brief clear-sky warming that could push maxima higher. Traders are therefore weighting outcomes toward the lower end of typical temperature bins, with resolution hinging on the final 24-hour maximum recorded at official Manila stations.
